name: CCW rotation (counterclockwise bimax rotation)

card.summary: A jaw-surgery technique in which the upper and lower jaw are moved together and rotated counterclockwise to bring the chin forward and give a longer, more defined jawline and lower face.
card.note: Major orthognathic surgery with weeks of recovery and risks including nerve numbness and infection.

quick.overview:
Counterclockwise (CCW) rotation is a way of planning bimaxillary jaw surgery. The maxilla and mandible are repositioned as a unit and tilted so the front of the bite moves up and the chin moves forward and up, rather than simply sliding the jaws straight forward.

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a route to a more projected chin, a sharper jaw angle and a more open facial profile for people with recessed or vertically long lower faces. Surgical literature studies it for skeletal Class II corrections and for airway enlargement in sleep apnea.
quick.how: The procedure is planned by an oral and maxillofacial surgeon with an orthodontist, usually with braces before surgery, 3D planning, and upper (Le Fort I) and lower (sagittal split) jaw osteotomies, sometimes with a chin procedure. Community members also discuss non-surgical approaches such as mouthguards, posture and growth-phase habits, which are anecdotal.
quick.risks: Orthognathic surgery involves general anaesthesia, swelling, a period on a soft or liquid diet, possible nerve numbness, infection and relapse of the jaw position. Reviews of mandibular CCW advancement note that studies are mostly retrospective case series. Candidacy depends on the individual anatomy and is decided with a surgeon.

lead: Counterclockwise (CCW) rotation refers to rotating the maxillomandibular complex, the upper and lower jaw moved together, in a counterclockwise direction when seen from the patient's right side. The movement raises the front of the bite and brings the chin forward and up, shortening the lower face's vertical height while increasing chin projection. Surgeons describe it within bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. [1][2]

On looksmax forums, CCW rotation is a frequently cited outcome of bimax surgery for people described as having downward-growing or recessed jaws. Posters discuss it alongside genioplasty and jaw implants as a hardmaxxing route to a stronger profile and larger airway. [3][4]

Published research examines CCW rotation for airway enlargement in obstructive sleep apnea, skeletal stability after mandibular advancement, and 3D airway volume changes. Appearance outcomes are the subject of surgical case series and community before-and-after posts.

paras: Orthognathic surgery corrects jaw and lower-face problems involving structure, bite, airway and appearance. Typical procedures include the bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) for the lower jaw, maxillary osteotomy for the upper jaw and genioplasty for the chin. [5]

CCW rotation is a way of combining these cuts: the jaws are advanced and tilted so the occlusal plane rotates, which changes chin position and jaw-angle appearance more than a straight advancement. [1]

Threads on looksmax.org ask how to get CCW rotation, whether it is possible at a given age, how short ramus affects it and how it combines with jaw implants and chin surgery. Some posters also discuss mouthguards, belt-pulling and puberty-phase habits as natural ways to influence rotation, which are community-reported and not reported in surgical literature. [3][4][6][7]

A 2018 meta-analysis found maxillomandibular advancement with CCW rotation produced significant increases in total upper airway volume and minimum axial area on CT. [1] A 2015 meta-analysis found large improvements in apnea-hypopnea index and lowest oxygen saturation after MMA with or without CCW rotation, though the sample was too small to compare techniques for pharyngeal volume. [8]

A 2019 systematic review of mandibular CCW rotational advancement for skeletal Class II deformity covered eight retrospective case series, all using rigid fixation, and examined postoperative stability. [2]

The studies above are systematic reviews of surgical cohorts and retrospective series; no randomized trial comparing aesthetic outcomes of CCW and non-rotational bimax surgery was found in the cited literature. [1][2][8]

General orthognathic risks include bleeding, swelling, infection (reported up to 7%) and nerve injury with facial numbness, which usually recovers within about three months but is occasionally permanent. Initial healing takes 2-6 weeks and bone healing a further 2-4 months. [5] Stability of mandibular advancement with rotation is a recognised research topic. [2]

lore.intro: CCW rotation is a common term in hardmaxxing threads on looksmax.org, where users discuss surgical and non-surgical routes to it. [3][4]

claims.claim: Bimax surgery with CCW rotation can transform a recessed profile
claims.believers: Posters share before-and-after photos and describe a more projected chin and sharper jaw after bimax with rotation. [4][9]
claims.experts: Surgical literature documents airway and skeletal changes after CCW advancement; appearance outcomes are reported mostly in case series. [1][2]

claims.claim: CCW rotation can be achieved naturally with a mouthguard or posture
claims.believers: Some users report results from mouthguards, belt-pulling or puberty habits and share personal progress posts. [6][10]
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing these methods for rotating the jaws in adults.
